applies_to: Any batch of newly published Indus inscriptions (e.g. Rakhigarhi 2013-16 seals, the Dholavira final report, CISI vol. 3.4) transcribed in Wells/ICIT sign numbers. Each prediction is checked on texts of 2+ signs that are complete at both ends.
authors: Erin Rae Toppe; prepared with Claude
frozen_lists: Openers, closers and numerals as frozen in hypotheses/H-2026-10-16-51b7445b.json; enclosure pairs as in hypotheses/H-2026-10-21-be9ab5ab.json.
note: Written before seeing any of the material. The sha256 of this JSON (without the sha256 field) is recorded in the commit that adds it.

predictions.claim: G740 (jar) is the most frequent final sign, and at least 55% of its occurrences are text-final.
Among texts whose first sign is a frozen opener, at least 60% end with a frozen closer.
G817 and G861 as first signs are followed by G2 at least 80% of the time and never by G60.
Signs carrying the four-corner enclosure strokes are in the end region more often than their unmarked bases.
On seals, a text model trained on ICIT predicts unicorn vs other animal with balanced accuracy below 0.60.
Numerals (frozen list) are not the final sign in at least 90% of their occurrences.
Texts without an opener start with a sign that is not in the frozen common-sign list more often than interior middle signs are uncommon.

No new site shows a regional vocabulary: a text model trained on ICIT seals cannot tell the new site's seals from Mohenjo-daro/Harappa seals better than chance (balanced accuracy below 0.60), given at least 30 new seals.

title: Sealed predictions for Indus inscriptions not yet published at sign level
